question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse mode for streamed tool calls, and must it wait for explicit per-tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and security-sensitive tool scheduling rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat early execution as blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract exists.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Leave current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering scheduling, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent file history ties steipete to the central agent-core and provider-stream surfaces that need the product and runtime-boundary decision.
